item.title: AI Policy Generalist
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/17/2026.

IMPORTANT SENSITIVE-CONTENT NOTICE: This role involves regular and deliberate engagement with sensitive material. Depending on the project, evaluations may include sexual content, emotional distress, self-harm, suicide, violence, weapons, abuse, exploitation, discrimination, and other potentially disturbing subjects. The work is conducted within structured evaluation frameworks and professional guidelines. Candidates must be able to engage with this material carefully, responsibly, and sustainably while maintaining sound judgment and consistent work quality.

Handshake AI supports frontier AI labs working on complex data at large scale. As an AI Policy Generalist, you will turn complex customer policies into consistent, well-reasoned evaluations of AI model behavior. You will read user requests, model responses, and relevant conversation history, then determine which policy category best applies. This is not rote annotation — policies cannot anticipate every possible edge case, and good evaluators do not apply them mechanically. The role requires balancing policy text and intent with customer expectations, conversation context, precedent, and team calibration. On-site in Seattle, WA, M-F, 8AM-5PM PT. W-2 classification. Compensation 5-5/hr.

Key responsibilities include: learning new customer policies, definitions, taxonomies, and evaluation rubrics quickly; evaluating user requests and AI model responses within the full relevant conversation context; distinguishing between closely related labels, severity levels, and policy boundaries; selecting the most defensible classification when a case is genuinely ambiguous; writing concise, evidence-based rationales that cite relevant policy language and conversation details; identifying policy gaps, contradictions, and unclear definitions; participating actively in calibration discussions with evaluators, project leads, policy teams, and researchers; challenging interpretations respectfully and updating judgment when new guidance or stronger reasoning emerges; and helping improve evaluation frameworks, examples, decision rules, and quality standards.

Qualifications: strong candidates may come from quality assurance, research, editing, law, teaching, operations, trust and safety, content moderation, social science, policy, investigations, compliance, or other fields that require careful interpretation and defensible decision-making. Key traits include the ability to make precise distinctions between cases, form and explain clear opinions, separate personal views from policy standards, and maintain accuracy during repetitive feedback-heavy work. Prior AI evaluation experience is helpful but not required. Experience with AI evaluation, data annotation, RLHF, model quality, trust and safety, or policy operations is a plus.

Compensation and logistics: 5-5/hr. W-2 classification. On-site in Seattle, WA. M-F, 8AM-5PM PT.

The Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) seeks a Policy Advisor (Program Specialist VII) within Access and Eligibility Services (AES). AES connects Texans to services and supports including food, medical care, cash assistance, and other social services. The Policy Advisor serves as team lead for the Texas Works Medicaid, Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), and Healthy Texas Women (HTW) policy staff, responsible for coordinating complex policy research and policy development support. Telework eligible. Up to 20% travel within Texas. 2+ years of policy experience required. Salary ,797.66-,900/month (9,571-4,800 annualized).

Key responsibilities include: planning and prioritizing policy for Texas Works Medicaid, CHIP, and HTW; developing and overseeing the development of policy options; performing advanced research on best practices and complex analysis of laws, regulations, and guidance; providing guidance, direction, and technical assistance to staff on the team; preparing high-quality briefing documents, issue papers, correspondence, bill analyses, and memoranda for senior and executive management; preparing and overseeing preparation of eligibility policies, agency rules, state plan amendments, and federal waivers; establishing, facilitating, and setting goals and objectives for multiple policy workgroups with staff from all impacted areas within HHS and external stakeholders; seeking guidance from and entering discussions with federal partners on interpretation of federal statute, rules, and regulations; and representing AES as a subject matter expert at business meetings, council and committee meetings, legislative meetings, and conferences.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in a relevant field preferred (relevant work experience may substitute on a year-for-year basis); at least 2 years of experience in policy writing, policy creation, or experience in Medicaid, CHIP, Healthy Texas Women, or other social service programs and policy; experience in policy development processes; experience writing, researching, interpreting, and analyzing complex data and policies; and experience synthesizing complex information and translating it into clear and concise policy documents. Knowledge of Texas Works Medicaid, CHIP, HTW, and other federal social service programs preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary ,797.66-,900/month (9,571-4,800 annualized). Comprehensive Texas state benefits including 100% paid employee health insurance for full-time eligible employees, defined benefit pension plan, and generous time off. Telework eligible. Austin, TX. Up to 20% travel within Texas. Application deadline: September 8, 2026.

item.title: (Senior) Research/Data Analyst, Housing Center
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/10/2026.

Note: The American Enterprise Institute (AEI) is a conservative, market-oriented policy research organization. AEI offers two openings at this level; final title (Research Analyst, Data Analyst, Senior Research Analyst, or Senior Data Analyst) and salary are commensurate with experience. A complete application must include a cover letter (demonstrating interest in housing policy and noting quantitative and technical experience), resume, unofficial academic transcript, and writing sample. Finalists will be asked to pass an analytical assessment. In-person in Washington, DC.

The AEI Housing Center is the nation's leading market-oriented housing research center, operating at the intersection of data-driven housing knowledge and policy solutions. The Research/Data Analyst will assist in creating, managing, and analyzing large datasets to derive insights and inform U.S. housing policy, including creating, cleaning, and analyzing new datasets; conducting statistical analyses; and helping draft research papers and other materials. A Research Analyst will focus more on researching and writing; a Data Analyst will focus more on analyzing data. A master's degree is preferred.

Key responsibilities include: performing statistical analysis and modeling to support studies and fulfill ad hoc requests; combining processes, techniques, and methodologies from various fields to perform predictive and statistical analysis on large and often disparate datasets; creating data listings, tabulations, graphs, and figures for studies and reports; integrating data from various sources; assembling financial, economic, and statistical datasets to inform comparative and predictive analyses of housing issues; examining data for trends and anomalies to draw actionable conclusions; and forecasting trends and deriving key indicators. Senior analysts will also develop models, algorithms, and metrics and apply deep professional knowledge to independently solve complex problems.

Qualifications: Research or Data Analyst: a master's degree with zero years of experience OR a bachelor's degree and at least two years of applicable experience; Senior Research/Data Analyst: a master's degree and at least one year of experience OR a bachelor's degree and at least three years of experience; a degree in economics, finance, real estate, public policy, computer science, or a related discipline; knowledge of Microsoft Excel; fluency in Stata, R, and Python; strong communication and organizational skills; a demonstrated interest in housing and public policy research; and strong understanding of statistical methods and data science techniques.

Compensation and logistics: salary $65,000-$85,000. Generous AEI benefits including 18 days paid leave, 12 sick days, paid family leave, medical/dental, health savings account, tuition assistance up to $5,200, life and disability insurance, and 403(b). In-person, Washington, DC. Cover letter, resume, unofficial transcript, and writing sample required.

item.company: BC Law – Initiative on Land, Housing & Property Rights
item.title: Policy Associate
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/10/2026.

Note: A J.D., master's degree, or another relevant graduate or advanced professional degree is required. This position is hybrid with a minimum of three days per week in the Initiative's office in Newton Centre, MA (Boston area). Some travel throughout the United States may be required. Apply via bc.csod.com (Boston College careers portal).

The Initiative on Land, Housing & Property Rights (ILHPR) at Boston College Law School addresses real property issues that impact poor and disadvantaged communities. The Initiative's Legal Reform and Policy Laboratory (the Lab) develops legal reform and policy proposals to address critical land and housing issues at the local, state, and federal level. A model of the Initiative's work is the Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act (UPHPA), a groundbreaking model state property statute that has been enacted into law in 27 states and jurisdictions. The Policy Associate will help further build up the Lab under the direction of the Policy Director. Salary $64,100-$80,100.

Key responsibilities include (60% Policy Work): monitoring local, state, and federal housing and other real property policies and identifying opportunities for the Initiative's engagement; conducting independent research on relevant topics, potential legal reform and policy projects, and relevant stakeholders; under the direction of the Policy Director, contributing to drafting and publishing policy reports and analyses of critical land and housing issues; supporting development of legal reform and policy proposals that can be implemented at the local, state, and/or federal level; and helping create policy-related presentations for conferences and other gatherings. (20% Strategy & Planning): helping develop and implement the Initiative's policy program workplan; monitoring progress of the workplan; supporting the Initiative's sponsorship of policy-related convenings including annual national conferences; and helping identify and cultivate partnerships with other organizations. (20% Administrative Responsibilities): assisting in securing financial resources and reporting progress to existing funders; helping coordinate Policy team projects; participating in coalitions with a complex and diverse group of stakeholders; and assisting with policy program convenings.

Qualifications: a J.D., master's degree, or another relevant graduate or advanced professional degree required; strong interpersonal and communications skills; excellent writing skills including strong technical citation skills; critical thinking and problem-solving skills; ability to manage multiple simultaneous projects and deadlines; and academic or work experience in the areas of rural or urban policy, affordable housing, heirs' property, land use, land conservation, economic justice, civil rights, environmental justice, or a related area.

Compensation and logistics: salary $64,100-$80,100 commensurate with relevant experience. Comprehensive Boston College benefits including tuition remission, generous medical/dental/vision, university-funded 401(k) and employer-sponsored 403(b), paid holidays, and generous sick and vacation pay. Hybrid in Newton Centre, MA (Boston area; minimum 3 days/week in office). Some U.S. travel required.

RBC Global Asset Management is seeking an Investment Policy Analyst to join its U.S. team in Stamford, CT. This role serves as a critical control function, ensuring investment activities comply with regulatory requirements and internal investment guidelines, focusing on portfolio adherence, front office advisory, and trade support. The position reports to the Investment Policy Manager. 0-3 years of experience. Salary $70,000-$120,000 plus variable compensation.

Key responsibilities include: supporting the Director and Investment Policy Manager with the design and implementation of RBC BlueBay's investment policy strategy and framework; providing practical guidance on global regulatory investment restrictions including Luxembourg UCITS, U.S. 1940 Act, and Canadian NI 81-102; management of the Charles River Investment Management System (CRIMS) and rules monitored outside CRIMS, including daily portfolio, pre- and post-trade alert management; onboarding new funds with a focus on negotiation of clear investment guidelines and subsequent monitoring; advising on the resolution of investment guideline breaches and trading issues; advising investment teams on regulatory and client guideline restrictions; development of management information and key risk indicators (KRIs) for senior leadership; and assisting with best execution monitoring and quarterly reporting of trade data.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree preferably in finance, economics, or accounting; 0-3 years of experience in investment policy/compliance, operations, or a related role within asset management; and basic understanding of fixed income fundamentals including bond mathematics, duration, yield curves, and credit spreads. Understanding of regulatory frameworks such as ERISA, SEC, Volcker, and the Investment Company Act of 1940 is a plus; proficiency with Charles River Investment Management System is a plus; and being on track to obtain a CFA designation is a plus.

Compensation and logistics: salary $70,000-$120,000 plus variable compensation through RBC's discretionary variable compensation program. item.title: Health Economics Research Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/10/2026.

Note: This is a fixed-term position with a current end date of June 30, 2027, which may be extended based upon available funding. No visa sponsorship. E-Verify. Hybrid eligible. Must reside and perform work in a state where Brown University is registered to do business (RI, CA, CO, CT, FL, MD, MA, NY, NH, NJ, NC, or DC).

The Health Economics Research Analyst at Brown University's School of Public Health (Department of Health Services Policy & Practice) joins a vibrant team supporting research to lower spending growth, improve patient outcomes, and drive structural change in U.S. health care delivery. Core topic areas include payment reform, long-term care, Medicare and Medicare Advantage, commercial price growth, health care market structures including the impacts of consolidation and private equity ownership, and state efforts to address affordability and value. The analyst will perform quantitative analyses for various center research projects, helping design studies, construct databases, manage data, perform statistical programming and analysis, and interpret and report results. Much of the work involves secondary data analysis of administrative datasets including health care claims.

Key responsibilities include: performing regression-based analyses using statistical software; working with large, complex datasets including health care claims data; constructing databases and managing data; conducting statistical programming and analysis; and communicating technical results clearly in written and graphical form.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree and 0-3 years of experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience; degrees in economics, applied economics, or closely related quantitative fields strongly preferred; hands-on experience implementing regression-based analyses using statistical software; training in econometrics and causal inference methods; experience working with large, complex datasets; strong attention to detail and ability to manage and validate data; and ability to communicate technical results clearly. Experience with administrative health care data (Medicare claims, commercial claims, or EHRs) preferred. No visa sponsorship.

Compensation and logistics: salary at Brown Grade 9 (see Brown's salary scale for reference). Comprehensive Brown benefits including generous PTO, medical/dental/vision starting day one, and retirement. Fixed-term through June 30, 2027 (may be extended). Hybrid eligible (must reside in a Brown-registered state). No visa sponsorship. E-Verify.

The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) is a non-profit, bipartisan public policy organization established in 1962 to provide strategic insights and practical policy solutions to decision makers concerned with global security and prosperity. The Economics and Security Technology (EST) Department advances policy research and dialogue at the intersection of economics, technology, national security, and global competitiveness. The Program Coordinator/Research Assistant (PCRA) will support the EST Front Office through program management, strategic communications, event coordination, research support, and stakeholder engagement. Must be eligible to work in Washington, DC and commit at least 35 hours per week. Salary $57,000-$65,000.

Key responsibilities include (Program Coordination and Front Office Operations): providing administrative, operational, and project management support to EST Front Office leadership; managing competing priorities and supporting multiple department-wide initiatives simultaneously; tracking project deliverables and deadlines; coordinating calendars, meetings, travel logistics, and stakeholder engagements; and supporting budget tracking, expense reporting, and administrative processes. (Research and Analysis): conducting policy and background research on economic security, technology, innovation, trade, energy, emerging technologies, and related policy issues; assisting with drafting reports, memos, briefing materials, presentations, and other research products; and monitoring key developments across EST issue areas. (Events, Roundtables, Forums, and Workshops): leading the planning and execution of public and private events, roundtables, workshops, conferences, podcasts, and strategic meetings; coordinating event logistics, speaker outreach, participant management, and post-event follow-up. (Strategic Communications and Stakeholder/Donor Engagement): supporting strategic communications efforts including social media content, newsletters, website updates, and podcasts; cultivating and maintaining relationships with policymakers, industry leaders, researchers, donors, and partner organizations; and assisting with fundraising activities including preparing and editing grant proposals, donor reports, and concept notes.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in public policy, international relations, economics, political science, business, communications, or a related field; strong qualitative and quantitative research and analytical skills; demonstrated interest in economic security, technology policy, innovation, energy, international affairs, or related policy issues; excellent written and verbal communication skills including executive-level writing; strong organizational, project management, and multitasking abilities; and proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, Salesforce, Pardot, Concur, Asana, and related collaboration tools.

Compensation and logistics: salary $57,000-$65,000. Washington, DC (in-person; minimum 35 hours/week). Must be eligible to work in Washington, DC.

item.title: Associate/Manager, Communications & Policy
item.description:
The Healthcare Anchor Network (HAN) exists to align hospitals nationwide around a common vision and practical framework for promoting economic inclusion and supporting local economies to create healthy, thriving communities. HAN catalyzes its 70 member health systems to individually and collectively leverage their institutional assets to maximize community impact. The Communications & Policy Associate/Manager will help conduct policy research, analysis, writing, and advocacy on social or structural determinants of health issues, particularly affordable housing, workforce development, and food security/systems, while also managing HAN's communications strategies. Note: this is a nonexempt, bargaining unit position covered by a collective bargaining agreement with the Nonprofit Professional Employees Union (NPEU). This is a full-time, remote position intended to start September 2026, with a 4-month probationary period (possible extension of 3 additional months). Application deadline: September 18, 2026. A resume/CV, detailed cover letter, and a 3-4 page writing sample are required.

Communications responsibilities include: participating in shaping overall communications strategy; providing communications support including writing/editing/storytelling, content support, design and visual content, presentation materials, reports, newsletters, and publications; supporting maintenance and updates of internal and external communications platforms including social media and digital content; and supporting leadership staff on preparation for presentations. Policy and advocacy responsibilities include: assisting with coordinating the HAN Aligning to Advance Policy initiative group; helping organize the HAN annual Policy Day; researching, analyzing, and writing policy documents; and government relations work.

Qualifications: a graduate degree or 5+ years of post-college work experience or relevant specialized skills/experience (7+ years for the manager position); proficiency in policy advocacy and communications including writing press releases and op-eds; proficiency in project management; and skilled and accomplished writing ability. Preferred: demonstrable familiarity with social determinants of health, the healthcare field, and anchor institution practices; experience with graphic design, content management, and social media management; and congressional or lobbying experience.

Compensation and logistics: starting salary Policy Associate III $67,682; maximum Project Manager II $89,994. Benefits include health care, three weeks paid vacation, and 7% employer 403(b) contribution (additional benefits governed by CBA). Fully remote. Application deadline: September 18, 2026. Start date: September 2026.

item.title: Health Policy Fellowship (ORISE)
item.description:
A fellowship opportunity is available in the Office of Health Policy within the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation (ASPE) at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) in Washington, DC. Note: this is an ORISE-administered fellowship (administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy). Participants do not become employees of HHS, DOE, or the program administrator -- this is a stipend, not a salary, and there are no employment-related benefits. U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency required. A master's or doctoral degree received within the past 5 years is required. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis; final deadline December 1, 2026.

The selected fellow will be mentored by a team of economic, policy, and public health experts who focus on healthcare markets, and will have opportunities to train with a wide range of data resources, collaborate on research studies, and engage in both quantitative and qualitative analytical projects in support of ASPE's priorities. Learning objectives include: developing and maintaining subject matter expertise in rural healthcare systems, Medicaid policy, and Health Insurance Marketplace financing and eligibility frameworks; analyzing regulations, legislation, executive directives, and policy reports; conducting and supporting research and program evaluation activities; synthesizing complex policy information into clear, actionable insights; and drafting professional correspondence, policy briefs, reports, presentations, and talking points.

Qualifications: a master's or doctoral degree in a relevant field (social science or related) received within the past five years; experience designing, planning, conducting, and communicating the results of analytical projects within economics or related fields; and knowledge of and experience with methodological and statistical techniques. The office has particular interest in applicants with experience in demography or actuarial science (not required). U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency required.

Compensation and logistics: monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience; stipend for healthcare benefits (not employer-sponsored benefits). One-year initial appointment, may be renewed contingent on funding. Full-time. Based in Washington, DC. Application deadline: December 1, 2026 (rolling reviews).
